what_was_built.library_kinds: reference, brand, project, playbook, experience, each a row in the registry and an independent `kb.library.kind` value
what_was_built.type_registry: kb.library_type: key, title, nullable description, template_version, allowed_extra_fields, review_process, is_core, retired_at. Five core types seeded by migration. Registering a sixth is an INSERT — no DDL, no migration of loaded sources.
what_was_built.grants: per-library roles via kb.library_grant, unchanged from 0002; the card adds the endpoints and the manager-only write path
what_was_built.projects: kb.project is a library of kind 'project' sharing one id, so the library role is the project role with no mapping table
what_was_built.links: kb.project_library_link — a requirement edge, with no principal column and no policy that consults the target library's role
what_was_built.pins: kb.project_rule_pin with PRIMARY KEY (project_id, rule_id) and FOREIGN KEY (rule_id, version_no); required by the new UNIQUE (id, version_no) on kb.rule
what_was_built.context: GET /projects/{id}/context returns a ProjectContext that is 'blocked' when any link or pin does not resolve, and carries no id, name, kind or text for the object that did not resolve

acceptance.type_and_audience_are_independent: test_kind_and_audience_are_independent_axes plus the four parametrised model cases in test_context_models.py: brand/all_invited, reference/private, project/all_invited and experience/invited are all accepted, and the two HTTP filters narrow independently
acceptance.pagination_and_counts_do_not_reveal_othe: test_counts_and_pages_describe_only_what_the_caller_may_see, test_the_stranger_sees_an_empty_catalogue_not_a_denied_one: `total` is count(*) OVER () of the identical RLS-scoped statement, and a page past the end still reports the true total

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.rule_action has no RLS policy. 0002 grants SELECT on all kb tables to kb_app, so any authenticated runtime principal can read every action step of every rule, in any library. C09 does not use that path: _actions_for() in src/kb/catalog/projects.py re-checks visibility with EXISTS against kb.rule (which is under FORCE RLS) and only ever passes rule ids that already resolved. Fixing the missing policy belongs to the owner of 0002.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: reported, not fixed — 0002 is outside this card's allowed paths

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: grant_write_manager is USING/WITH CHECK on the effective role, so the creator of a new library cannot insert their own first manager grant: a library that does not exist yet has no effective role for anybody. Any card that creates a library through the runtime role hits this.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: worked around narrowly in 0003 with kb.create_owned_library(), a SECURITY DEFINER function that inserts exactly the library row and the caller's own manager grant, forces p_principal = current_principal(), refuses a session with no principal, and has a fixed search_path. A single-owner alternative would be a policy that admits a grant where the caller is about to become the manager.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.project_rule_pin rows are readable by any reader on the project and therefore expose one opaque rule UUID per pin, including pins whose rule the caller cannot read. The rule's title, text, kind and library stay behind kb.rule's RLS and the API never returns the id of a pin it could not resolve. The alternative — keying the pin policy on the rule too — would make a mandatory pin vanish from the manifest, shrink the count to match, and let the project report a complete context while withholding a brand rule, which is the A12 failure. The project-scoped read is the lesser exposure and the intended one.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: documented in the migration and in the module docstring; behaviour asserted in test_a_pinned_rule_the_caller_cannot_read_blocks_the_context

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.library.kind is a PostgreSQL ENUM and enums are closed, so a type registered through the API is known to the registry and the catalogue before it can back a library. Attaching one needs the enum value added by the DDL owner. This is the one part of ARCHITECTURE.md §4's 'extend by configuration' that the schema cannot deliver, and it is stated in the migration rather than papered over.
